subject: ventures/paver-patio-bid-calculator
professional: a hardscape contractor who bids residential paver patios, walkways and driveway pads; first checks: does the base yardage match what the supplier will actually deliver (loose vs compacted, yards vs tons, base carried past the edge), is haul-away priced on swelled spoil, are base depths in the ICPI pedestrian/vehicular ranges, is waste material and cut time labor, is margin taken on price, and does a cleared box ever price as zero

evidence.correctness: Five bids recomputed in an independent Python script (/tmp/claude-0/paver_check.py, own formulas: cu yd = sq ft x in / 324, ceil bags, loaded wage, overhead on direct, price = cost / (1 - margin)) and compared with calculateBid run from node (/tmp/claude-0/paver_run.mjs): README default 12x16 running bond 5.556 cu yd, 20.938 h, cost $3,417.26, price $4,381.10, $22.82/sf; 45-degree herringbone on 10 in $4,017.92 / $5,151.18 / $26.83; vs-a-flat patio without haul $3,065.87 / $3,930.60 / $20.47; 20x24 circular driveway $9,259.22 / $11,870.79, flat-rate quote 480 x 20.4719 = $9,826.50, realized margin 5.77%; own 14x22 90-degree herringbone on 4 in base, $28 wage, 25% burden, no haul $4,317.10 / $5,534.74. All match to the cent. Capped at 2: a blank field priced silently as zero (blank wage $3,096.92 with no labor, blank margin priced at cost $3,417.26, blank paver cost $3,018.08), and the base and haul yardage are in-place volumes a supplier and a dump do not bill on (see domain): with a 1.25 compaction factor, 1.25 spoil swell and 6 in base extension the default patio costs $3,677.64 and prices $4,714.93, 7.6% above the tool.
evidence.completeness: README features checked end to end: four job presets, pattern and use presets with the edited-field guard, haul toggle, proposed-price check, copy bid summary (formatBidSummary run), share link (share.mjs round trip tests), printable proposal with deposit and validity (proposal.mjs, proposal-terms.mjs suites), usage tally with DNT/GPC opt-out (usage.mjs). All seven README events are count() calls in index.html. Served copy (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs) leaves no placeholder origin in llms.txt, sitemap or canonicals. No stubs or TODOs found.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/paver-patio-bid-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 136/136 pass at start (139/139 after the fixes here). Eight seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: six engine mutants caught (paver thickness dropped from excavation depth, haul on base yards, ceil -> round on bags, install hours on bought pavers, margin guard >= -> >, entered edge ignored); two survived: belowBreakEven < -> <= (equality boundary only) and index.html:527 forcing the pattern-change to overwrite a hand-edited waste % (the page's edited-field guard has no test). The blank-field bug had no test.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (335 lines, pure, documented), index.html script (readInput, update, applyPreset, pattern/use handlers), share.mjs (allowlisted keys, safe decode), vs-* pages and tests. Clean engine with explicit validation; defects: number() accepted '' as 0, the money formatter is duplicated in calc.mjs:313 and index.html:340, and page behaviour lives in an inline module with only static-text tests.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer present on every page; no-upload privacy matches usage.mjs. README and guide figures ($4,381.10, $22.82, 20.9 h, $3,417.26, $5,151.18, $26.83, 5.6 vs 7.9 cu yd, 56 vs 88 ft edge) all reproduce. vs-a-flat figures reproduce. Not backed: the index FAQ (visible and JSON-LD) said a 10 in driveway 'digs out and hauls off roughly two-thirds more material'; the engine's own excavation is 7.926 / 5.556 = 43% more (the base stone is 67% more), and it said excavation comes 'from area and base depth' when it is base + bedding + paver. vs-aspire.html said Aspire plans are 'tiered by a contractor's annual revenue' and 'its site describes plans as scaled to a contractor's annual revenue' (lines 6, 12, 52, 58, 85, 92, 103) while its own test admits the pricing page was never reached; the 2026-11-13 snow-removal audit fetched youraspire.com and found /pricing 404 and no revenue-tier text. Other Aspire facts (Chesterfield MO, Kehoe and Tipton, ServiceTitan 2021, no published price) are backed by that fetch; 'founded in 2013' is half-backed (the site says 2013 and 2014) and 'commercial cleaning contractors' is not backed by any file. youraspire.com is 403 through this session's proxy, so I could not re-check.
evidence.fitness: Walked a contractor's job: a 14x22 herringbone patio priced in under a minute with a printable proposal and walk-away. What they hit in the first hour: the gravel yardage is not what they order (no compaction factor, no tons option, no base extension past the edge), haul-away is on bank yards, a cleared box priced silently, and only one rectangle per takeoff (steps, seat walls, curves are folded into edge feet and waste, as the README says).
evidence.domain: Against ICPI-style installation guidance (ICPI Tech Spec 2 / installer manuals): compacted aggregate base 4-6 in for pedestrian and 8-12 in for residential vehicular, about 1 in of bedding sand, base extended beyond the paver edge by at least the base thickness, edge restraint on all sides. The tool's 6 in / 10 in and 1 in bedding sit inside those ranges and waste-as-material with a separate cut-labor factor is how estimators work; 7/10/15/18% waste matches common trade starting points. Departures: the base is excavated and priced only under the finished face (no extension), base is priced on compacted volume with no loose-to-compacted factor (crushed aggregate typically needs 20-30% more loose yards, or about 1.4 t per loose yd), and spoil haul uses in-place volume with no swell (soil bulks about 25%). Each biases the bid low.

defects.what: A blank field (or '1,200', which a number input sanitizes to '') priced as zero with no error: blank wage $3,096.92 with no labor, blank margin priced at cost, blank paver cost dropped the pavers

Base stone priced on compacted in-place cubic yards with no loose/compaction factor or tons option, haul-away on bank volume with no swell, and the base not extended past the paver edge as ICPI-style guidance recommends; together the default patio is 7.6% low ($4,381.10 vs $4,714.93)

Index FAQ (visible and JSON-LD) said a 10 in driveway 'digs out and hauls off roughly two-thirds more material' than a 6 in patio; the engine digs 43% more (only the base stone is 67% more), and said excavation comes 'from area and base depth' rather than base + bedding + paver

vs-aspire.html asserted Aspire plans are tiered by annual revenue and that 'its site describes plans' that way, while its own test admits the pricing page was never reached; youraspire.com/pricing was 404 with no such text when an earlier audit fetched it
The page's edited-field guard (a pattern change must not overwrite a hand-edited waste %) has no test: forcing the overwrite survived all 136 tests
One rectangle per takeoff and no geotextile, steps, seat walls or sealing lines; curves and borders only through edge feet and waste (partly stated in README Limitations)
vs-aspire says Aspire serves 'commercial cleaning contractors' and was 'founded in 2013' with no file or fetched source behind the first, and the vendor's own site giving 2013 and 2014 for the second
The money formatter is duplicated between calc.mjs and the page script

verdict: Below the bar, on correctness and claims, not on arithmetic. The engine reproduces five independently computed bids to the cent, including every figure on the README, guide and flat-rate page, and its tests are strong: six of eight seeded engine mutants fail a test. What a hardscape estimator would hit first: the gravel line is compacted in-place yards priced as if a supplier sold them that way, spoil is hauled at bank volume, and the base stops at the paver edge, so the default patio is about 7.6% low against ICPI-style practice; a cleared box priced as zero; the driveway FAQ overstated the extra dig-out (43%, not two-thirds); and the Aspire page asserted revenue-tiered pricing it never checked. In this session the blank-field bug, the FAQ ratio and the Aspire revenue claim were fixed in the subject with tests (139/139); the yardage model and the untested page guard are recorded as known gaps in the README. Scores are before those fixes.
